A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same human and LLM plausibility-judgment study despite the changed title. The complete main text, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved between sections.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments collecting 3,000 human and 13,600 LLM plausibility judgments, with rating comparisons, significance tests, regression analyses, and appendix examples.

after.justification: v3 retains these original human and LLM experimental results and analyses in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The GPT-4o rationale-generation procedure, model-selection study, human rating procedure, and LLM prompting remain unchanged. Appendix A.5 retains the same six prompts.

E1.justification: Both versions use Social IQA and CommonsenseQA, gold and distractor answers, and NO, PRO, CON, and PRO+CON rationale conditions. The SIQA preference pilot and US-based English-speaking annotator population are also retained.

E2.justification: The four rationale-generation candidates, 17 LLM raters grouped into OpenAI and Non-OpenAI models, human comparisons, and NO-rationale control are unchanged.

E3.justification: Both retain 50 questions per dataset, two selected answers per question, five human judgments per rationale condition, and the same rating scale and decoding settings. Moving the regression-centering explanation from a footnote into Section 5 does not change the protocol.

E4.justification: The regressions examining initial ratings, rationale type, and rationale length remain unchanged, as do the case examples in Tables 6–9. Relocating Table 4 adds no analysis.

E5.justification: Both retain the single-run disclosure in Appendix A.3, chi-squared homogeneity tests, and t-test significance markings in Tables 4–5. No repeated-run or uncertainty-reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: The numerical results in Tables 2–9 and distributions in Figures 2–3 are unchanged. For example, the SIQA human gold-answer PRO rating remains 3.84, a change of −0.26 from the NO-rationale condition.

T1.justification: No mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised. The regression variables and centering remain identical; the new Grice discussion provides conceptual interpretation rather than formal theory.

C1.justification: The central empirical contributions remain unchanged. However, the conclusion extends the earlier general concern about psychological influence with a specific conjecture that manipulation risk might be higher in specialized or technical domains.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 connects the existing 'underselling' explanation to Grice's Maxim of Quantity and elaborates a doubt-induced downgrading mechanism. The conclusion adds interpretations about users prioritizing LLM arguments over their knowledge and failing to notice manipulation. Existing limitations remain.

D1.justification: Footnote 1 changes from promising future data and code release to stating that data are available and providing a repository link. Code release is no longer explicitly promised. Appendix implementation details are unchanged; repository contents cannot be established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v3 adds Grice, availability-heuristic literature, and Batista and Griffiths (2026) on belief distortion, modestly expanding its psychological context. Existing novelty positioning remains. The Chen and Lee reference changes update previously cited works to their published versions.

P1.justification: v3 changes the title, explicitly mentions LLM judges in the opening framing, expands selected explanatory and concluding passages, and adds acknowledgements. The regression-centering footnote becomes body text; the overall narrative and section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Table 4 moves from the appendix on v2 PDF page 13 to the main text on v3 PDF page 8. Prompt blocks are repaginated and printed page numbers disappear. The figures and table designs otherwise remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 provides concrete data-access instructions, brings Table 4 closer to its discussion, and connects the underselling hypothesis to relevant literature. These modest gains improve accessibility and exposition while preserving the empirical evidence. The new mechanism and manipulation-risk discussion remains untested, and code availability is less explicit, limiting the overall improvement.
